## Arrows That Point One Way
*Plan (1 page). Findings: which relation patterns (symmetric, antisymmetric, inverse, compositional) each knowledge-graph model can and cannot express, in the order in which each fixed what the previous one could not: translation, bilinear products, rotation. Achieved for the representation of meaning: difference as a relation (@sec-prop-difference), with a direction for each relation. Computation: whether embeddings learned from data make explicit graph structure unnecessary, or graph and vector converge into one system, read from cost per query and quality at matched data, dated. Evidence at scale: re-evaluations in which older knowledge-graph models match newer ones once they are trained with equal tuning are reported (from memory, unchecked: Ruffinelli et al. 2020), the same lesson as the comparison of counting and predicting in @sec-ch-embedding-spaces, and the chapter says what a new model has to show against a tuned baseline. Smoke test: TransE, DistMult, ComplEx and RotatE on a toy graph with one relation of each pattern, where a model that cannot express a pattern must fail on it, a check with an analytic answer (TransE is in references/). Still out of reach: a pairwise edge cannot express a relation among three or more things, and the prerequisite order of a subject is a graph that a space has to recover (the dependency question of the critical literacy test). Multi-way interactions are taken up in @sec-ch-topological-deep-learning.*
